name: spaces
title: Spaces
description: The pages slide across as one strip, the way macOS switches desktops: a spring, a gap, a lift, and direction from your route order. No dependencies — the stylesheet drives it.
docs:
Wrap your layout with the transition. This is the only step:

  // app/layout.tsx
  import { SpacesTransition } from "@/components/spaces"

  export default function RootLayout({ children }) {
    return (
      <html lang="en">
        <body>
          <SpacesTransition routes={["/", "/work", "/about"]}>{children}</SpacesTransition>
        </body>
      </html>
    )
  }

Your existing <Link>s and <a>s are intercepted automatically.

The two pages travel as one strip with a thin gap between them, on a real
damped spring: fast out of the gate, a long soft landing. As they move they
lift off the surface, take on rounded corners and lean into the direction of
travel, and settle back flat and square as they land. The incoming page trails
by a frame so the gap breathes.

routes is your pages in order, left to right. A navigation to a page further
along slides left; further back slides right. Anything not listed uses
direction. gap, lift, radius, bank, lag and bounce each tune one part of the
motion and can be zeroed.

Colour: backdrop="dark" (default) or "light" sets what shows in the gap. For
anything else pass backdrop="custom" and set --spaces-backdrop and
--spaces-glow yourself in components/transitions.css.

Requires the View Transitions API (Chrome 111+, Safari 18+, Firefox 132+).
Older browsers navigate normally with no animation. Browser back/forward is
not animated.
